Synopsis:
    Icelandic voters rejected (52.8% vs 47.2%) the government's proposal to reopen EU accession talks. In response, Iceland's foreign minister signalled the country will pursue alternative security arrangements via bilateral agreements and deeper EEA cooperation. The backdrop is heightened Arctic geopolitical tension driven by Trump's Greenland ambitions and uncertainty over US NATO commitment. Iceland remains in the EEA and holds a 1951 bilateral defence agreement with the US, but has no standing army.
